All hr 0. (b) FAILURE MODE: NeRF per-scan neural attenuation field, REGIME-BOUNDED on DENSE 2304-view Mayo (LD-FBP near-complete -> hr structurally 0 vs ~0.81 cal floor); per-scene INR capacity-bound ~0.696 SSIM in the 5.0s/scene budget; hash payoff lives in the 128-view SPARSE regime, not dense Mayo. (c) THE 0.6964->0.7376 ITER-16 QUESTION = THROUGHPUT VARIANCE, NOT SIGNAL. Verified from observations: cfg BYTE-IDENTICAL (per_scene_s=5.0, outer_wall_s=1080, n_iter=3000), elapsed flat 1096-1103s, BUT val_n (scenes that finished per-scene fitting within the FIXED outer wall) tracks SSIM MONOTONICALLY: iter-9 val_n194->0.6803, iters8/10-14 val_n200-203->0.693-0.696 band, iter-15 val_n200->0.6964, ITER-16 val_n206->0.7376. On a less-loaded GPU MORE scenes complete (and more optimizer steps/scene) under the fixed wall -> higher mean SSIM over the finished subset. This is exactly the wall-clock step-count sensitivity the iter-16 subagent predicted. 0.7376 is a SCHEDULING ARTIFACT, NOT a config gain. (d) DECISION: EMPTY-PATCH {} is CORRECT - every in-budget monotone axis is mapped (width EXHAUSTED, feat_dim LIFTED-to-ceiling, levels SATURATED, lr REGRESSED); the only untouched lever-class is the wall/step-count B-fix (naf_per_scene_s/naf_outer_wall_s) DELIBERATELY HELD CONSTANT iters6-16 for comparability - changing it would change step-count and break the lineage, so it stays an OUT-OF-PROTOCOL deferred knob, not an in-budget move. (e) BUDGET: identical cfg, elapsed ~1096-1103s, inside 30-min kill / 20-min governor. (f) BASE_ITER=15 (NOT iter-16): iter-15 is the canonical iter-8-lineage cfg at the top of the GENUINE 0.693-0.696 noise band under representative GPU load (val_n=200); iter-16s 0.7376 is throughput-inflated (val_n=206) and basing on it would silently carry a wall-clock artifact forward as a false best and pollute the comparable lineage. HARD-WIRED unchanged: val_n=214 ALL L277, staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geom, per-sample-ps, bg_target=truth, 321px FOV default, no fov override. PREDICT SSIM ~0.696 (0.693-0.697 genuine noise band; ignore any new throughput-driven outlier), hr 0. Documents the regime-bounded hash-NAF deterministic ceiling toward iter-20 and the val_n-throughput confound for future readers.
